title: autofix.config.json
description: Configuration for the dev-autofix plugin. Generated by /dev-autofix:init, read by /dev-autofix:run and /dev-autofix:plan.

version.description: Config format version. Bumped only on a breaking change.

reservePercent.description: Percent of the weekly budget to leave untouched. A run stops when weekly used >= 100 - reservePercent.

fiveHourCeiling.description: Stop when the 5-hour window is at or above this percent used.

maxFixesPerRun.description: Hard cap on PRs opened in a single /dev-autofix:run invocation.

maxSnapshotAgeSeconds.description: Maximum age of each available window's observation (observed5 or observed7). An idle status-line refresh does not renew observations; stale windows need a new API reading.

perFixPercentEstimate.description: Starting estimate of budget percent one fix consumes, used to size parallel waves (with a 2x safety factor). Limits the risk of crossing the reserve; cannot guarantee it, since a fix's cost is not known in advance. Replaced by the largest observed per-fix delta during a run.

fallbackSearch.description: When a repo has no ready queue entry, let the worker search for its own candidate (verification failures, audit documents, TODO/FIXME). Off by default: unplanned work skips the human review of the backlog.

blockPatterns.description: Extra regular expressions that must not appear on any added line of a fix. Added to the built-in malware signatures checked by the push gate. A match stops the run.

disabledPatterns.description: Ids of built-in push-gate patterns to switch off. Malware signatures (a match stops the run): global-bang, fromcharcode-127, auth-api-key, auth-confirm-nine, trongrid, bsc-dataseed, aptoslabs, atob-env, config-bat. Risky constructs (a match blocks that one entry): create-require, eval, new-function. Use when a repository legitimately contains one.

protectedPaths.description: Extra regular expressions, matched against the repo-relative path, for files no fix may touch in any repo (e.g. "^db/migrations/"). Added to the built-in list of dependency manifests, lockfiles, CI and hook config, scripts and build files.

deployPatterns.description: Regular expressions for deploy or manual steps. When a queue entry names a command matching one, publish refuses a PR body that does not repeat it. Set to [] to switch the check off.

workerModel.description: Model for fix workers. Planning inherits the lead model.

finishModel.description: Model for the worker that addresses review comments in /dev-autofix:finish. That work needs more judgement than executing a plan.

reviewers.description: GitHub logins whose PR comments /dev-autofix:finish acts on. Defaults to the authenticated gh user. Comments from anyone else are never acted on.

approveTokens.description: Approval tokens. A pending comment that is exactly one of these (case-insensitive), alone or followed by a `Reviewed head: <sha>` line, is an approval; /dev-autofix:finish merges when every pending comment is an approval and the newest is bound to the current head. Anything else is treated as concerns to address.

maxDiffLines.description: A fix whose diff grows past this is blocked and preserved for re-scoping.

queuePath.description: Path to the backlog file, relative to the directory holding this config. /dev-autofix:plan writes it; /dev-autofix:run consumes it.

worktreeRoot.description: Directory for reusable worktrees, preserved recoveries and planning scratch. Must be outside every repo checkout, or the checkout's typecheck, lint and test globs pick up the worktree copies.

usageSnapshotPath.description: Where the status line writes the budget snapshot.

coAuthor.description: Appended as a Co-Authored-By trailer on every autofix commit. Omit for no trailer.

sources.description: Repo-relative or absolute paths to audit documents the planner mines for candidates (code-smell inventories, warning plans, architecture reviews). Paths are relative to the directory holding this config.

forbidden.description: Extra hard rules appended verbatim to every worker and investigator brief, on top of the built-in safety rules.

repos.description: Repositories in scope. Each gets its own single-occupancy worktree.

name.description: Short identifier, used for the worktree directory and in reports.

path.description: Absolute path to the user's main checkout. Never modified; only used as the worktree source. Use forward slashes on Windows.

remote.description: GitHub owner/repo slug, used for `gh pr create` and open-PR dedupe.

baseBranch.description: Branch to base fixes on and target with PRs (e.g. main, staging).

install.description: Dependency install command, run in a fresh worktree or when the lockfile hash changes. Install scripts are skipped by default because a poisoned dependency runs through them; a repo that needs one package built can append `&& npm rebuild <package>`, which runs only that package's scripts.

lockfile.description: File hashed to decide whether a reinstall is needed.

prepare.description: Commands run once per fresh worktree before verification (codegen, type generation).

verify.description: Required nonempty commands that must pass before a PR is opened or merged. Keep these fast and non-interactive.

commandTimeoutSeconds.description: Per-command timeout for worktree preparation, local review and merge verification's install, prepare and verify commands. Runs with CI=1; timeout terminates the command process group and records failure.

forbidden.description: Hard rules for this repo only (for example its own CLAUDE.md rules), appended to worker and investigator briefs after the global forbidden list.

protectedPaths.description: Extra regular expressions for files no fix may touch in this repo, added to the global protectedPaths.

env.description: Extra environment variable names (never values) passed through to install, prepare and verify commands, e.g. DATABASE_URL or NPM_TOKEN. Both dev-autofix and dev-autotask run those commands with a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, locale, temp and package-manager cache variables, CI=1), so anything not listed here is absent.

testCommand.description: Optional command template for running tests covering touched files. `{files}` is replaced with the changed paths. Omit if the repo has no unit test runner.
